prompt.role: You are a senior mobile product designer specializing in fitness apps. Redesign the ARCH calisthenics training app — a dark-themed React Native app targeting serious bodyweight athletes. Think Freeletics meets Apple Fitness+ with a more aggressive, technical aesthetic.
design_principles: Action-first: users should start training in ≤ 2 taps from home
Readability under duress: large, high-contrast text for timers and sets (user is moving/sweating)
Cognitive load reduction: one clear purpose per screen, no duplicate data across tabs
Visual > Textual: use icons, progress rings, color coding instead of text labels where possible
Purposeful motion: animations for functional feedback only (set completion, rest timer, streak increment)

home.name: Home
home.purpose: Get the user training as fast as possible
current_issues: Too many sections competing for attention
Stats (XP, workouts, streak) shown on Home + Profile — redundant
Intelligence insights panel feels like bloat
Program structure panel duplicates what's in Train tab

redesign_direction.hero: Full-width greeting with daily readiness score (Recovery %) as a large ring or gauge — this is the hero, not text
redesign_direction.streak: Fire emoji + streak count, compact, no full-width bar
redesign_direction.daily_mission: One card: 'Today's Focus: [muscle group]' with a visual body-map thumbnail showing the target area in accent color
redesign_direction.train_button: Massive, thumb-zone CTA — gradient from #F59E0B to #D97706, minimum 56px height, with a chevron icon. This is the #1 element on screen
redesign_direction.remove: Stats grid, intelligence panel, exercise library shortcut, program structure — all moved or deleted

train.name: Train
train.purpose: Show today's workout and let the user start
current_issues: Program structure panel duplicates data from the training system
Difficulty selector adds unnecessary decision point
Too much text explaining progression when visual would suffice

redesign_direction.recommendation: Top card: AI recommendation with muscle group icons (colored dots or body silhouettes), not text paragraphs
redesign_direction.progression: Compact horizontal progress bar (set 3/12) with the next progression level shown as a small badge, not a full panel
redesign_direction.workout_cards: Stack of 3-4 workout cards with: exercise thumbnail/icon, name, set×rep count, and a colored difficulty dot (green/yellow/red)
redesign_direction.remove: Program structure panel, difficulty selector, verbose progression text

history.name: History
current_issues: Charts and stats compete for attention
Session list is dense and hard to scan

redesign_direction.summary_hero: Top section: 3 big numbers in a row — Total Workouts, Current Streak, Total Volume — with subtle trend arrows (↑↓) in accent color
redesign_direction.chart: Single line chart for weekly volume, minimal — no gridlines, just the curve with a gradient fill below
redesign_direction.sessions: Scrollable list of session cards: date, duration, exercise count, and a colored dot for intensity. No stat modules per session
redesign_direction.remove: Multiple chart types, redundant stat displays

body_map.name: Body Map
body_map.purpose: Visual muscle group overview — unique differentiator

redesign_direction.silhouette: Center-stage body silhouette with color-coded muscle groups: green = recently trained, yellow = ready, red = needs recovery, gray = untouched
redesign_direction.tap_interaction: Tap a muscle group → slide-up sheet with: last trained date, total sets this week, recommended next exercise (with thumbnail)
redesign_direction.remove: Grid of muscle group names — the silhouette IS the interface, not a supplement to it

profile.name: Profile
profile.purpose: Settings and account — keep it boring
current_issues: Exercise progression section is detailed but rarely visited

redesign_direction.identity: Avatar + name + level badge (e.g., 'LVL 12 — INTERMEDIATE') — this is the hero
redesign_direction.compact_stats: One row: 🏋️ 47 workouts · 🔥 12 streak · ⚡ 24.5K XP — just numbers, no StatModule components
redesign_direction.settings: Clean list with icons: Account, Notifications, Video Cache, Theme, About
redesign_direction.remove: Full stats grid, recent activity section (that's what History is for), detailed exercise progression

workout_screen.purpose: The core experience — must be flawless during physical activity

redesign_direction.timer: Full-screen countdown timer during rest periods — giant monospaced font, accent color, haptic pulse at 3-2-1
redesign_direction.exercise_name: Large, bold, at top — user needs to read this from 2 meters away
redesign_direction.rep_counter: Center of screen, massive number, with +/- buttons in thumb zone
redesign_direction.form_guide: Collapsible panel at bottom — tap to expand exercise tips, but DEFAULT to collapsed (don't clutter the workout)
redesign_direction.next_exercise: Small preview card at bottom: 'Next: [exercise name] [icon]' — reduces anxiety about what's coming
redesign_direction.completion: Full-screen celebration animation on workout finish — confetti, total time, total volume, streak maintained

typography.heading: Bebas Neue — all caps, letter-spacing 2-4px
typography.timer: Monospaced or tabular numbers, minimum 48pt during workout

design_system.shadows: Minimal — use elevation/surface color difference instead of drop shadows

navigation.layout: Bottom tab bar with icons + short labels
navigation.notes: Remove Body Map as a tab — integrate it into the Train screen or as a modal. 4 tabs is cleaner than 5.

references: Freeletics: AI coach module, streak gamification, minimal text
Apple Fitness+: rings-centric progress, studio-quality workout UI
Nike Training Club: community-driven, visual workout browsing
Calimove: skill progression systems, technical calisthenics focus
constraints: Must work on both iOS and Android
Offline-first: workout data must be available without internet
Dark theme only — no light mode
